newsitem.title: USA: S&P sees stable rating for Venezuela over 1-2 yrs.
newsitem.headline: S&P sees stable rating for Venezuela over 1-2 yrs.

text.p: U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's, which raised Venezuela's sovereign debt ceiling on Thursday, said the country's B-plus long term foreign currency rating would likely remain constant over the next year or two.
S&P director of sovereign ratings Lacey Gallagher told Reuters Financial Television the rating accounted for what the agency considered possible during the next elections in 1998.
"This is a fairly stable rating for Venezuela over a one-two year time horizon, although very significant progress on these issues, including inflation, could strengthen Venezuela's credit standing."

Gallagher said she did not see much likelihood for a viable macroeconomic stabilization fund before the next elections but considered as more probable that Congress would complete further privatizations and labor law reform.
"The rating factors in what we think is possible during the next year or so," Gallagher said.
"Progress on (these issues) would not be inconsistent with a B-plus foreign currency rating," she said.
Gallagher said the new rating also factored in the risk of a currency devaluation, which could complicate the inflation scenario.
On Thursday, S&P raised Venezuela's long term debt rating to B-plus from single B.
